profiles.Summary: FTL: Faster Than Light is a lightweight 2D indie strategy game from 2012 that runs effortlessly on the Steam Deck, well within the hardware's capabilities. It is rated Playable on Deck (likely due to minor UI/controller quirks) but performs flawlessly at full speed with minimal power draw.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's minimal 2012 PC requirements, its 2D engine nature, and the Deck hardware. On first run, confirm the game launches in fullscreen and that the UI is readable — if text is too small, use the Deck's touchscreen or enable magnification in Steam settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: FTL is extremely light on resources; a 4 W TDP and low GPU clock are more than sufficient. The 30 fps cap at 40 Hz keeps battery life very long — ideal for travel or low-power sessions.

KnownIssues: Controller/gamepad support is limited — mouse and keyboard input via the touchscreen or trackpad is recommended for best experience.
Steam Deck Verified status is 'Playable' rather than 'Verified', suggesting some UI elements may be small or require touchscreen interaction.
No native Linux build is available; the game runs via Proton, though platinum ProtonDB reports indicate no significant compatibility issues.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapping TDP and GPU clock offers no real benefit for this 2D title — the game is CPU/logic-bound and will sit at 60 fps regardless. Useful if you want zero overhead for alt-tabbing or streaming.

Optimal.Notes: A 60 fps cap at native resolution with a modest 5 W TDP limit gives a perfectly smooth experience while still keeping battery life excellent. Integer scaling preserves the pixel-art aesthetic cleanly at 1280x800.

The game is rated Playable (not Verified) primarily due to its small UI and text scaling on the Deck's screen, but it is otherwise fully functional and stable under Proton.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's 2012 2D engine, its very low PC minimum requirements, and the Steam Deck hardware. On first launch, confirm the Proton layer starts correctly, then check that text and UI are legible — if they are too small, try the in-game resolution or zoom options, or use the Deck's built-in magnifier.

MaxBattery.Notes: FTL is a 2D game with near-zero GPU demand; a 3 W TDP and minimal GPU clock are more than sufficient. The 30 fps cap is used here purely to minimise power draw — the game is a slow-paced strategy title where low frame rates are imperceptible.

KnownIssues: UI elements and text can appear small on the 1280x800 screen, as the game was designed for mouse and keyboard
No native controller support — on-screen controls or community controller layouts are needed
The game is marked Playable rather than Verified, likely due to UI/input concerns rather than performance or stability issues

MaxPerformance.Notes: FTL's engine caps effective output well below 90 fps in practice, so the OLED's 90 Hz refresh is largely symbolic here; the game will feel identical to 60 Hz. There is genuinely no performance ceiling to push against — this profile exists for completeness, and the Optimal profile is the better daily driver.
